# nmrML schema test input

`nmrML.xsd` is copied unchanged from the official nmrML project:
https://github.com/nmrML/nmrML/blob/99b854e7dc61ca85fcae16a068691dde160fa012/xml-schemata/nmrML.xsd

SHA-256: `f4995a9891ca00079fa0d885d0f4f8291ee712ee956fdd6932740d3df3a39117`.
The schema declares version `1.0.rc1`; the live versioned schema URL returned
the same bytes during qualification. The upstream MIT licence is preserved in
`LICENSE.nmrML`. No experimental spectra are distributed here. Synthetic
metadata and binary samples are generated by the tests.

XSD validation tests require optional xmltodict and lxml. Structural XSD
validation does not validate controlled-vocabulary semantics, chemical
calibration, endpoint conventions or the correctness of original instrument
conversions. The original public hop and Bayesil examples fail this XSD and
remain external, checksum-pinned local qualification inputs.

`synthetic.nmrML` is an original synthetic eight-point raw + processed document,
generated by `document()` in `tests/fileio/test_nmrml.py` and the writer. Samples
are the complex numbers 0 through 7. It is licensed with this repository and
validated against the pinned XSD; it contains no measured data or identities.

`synthetic-2d-real.nmrML` is an original synthetic processed reference under
the repository license. The pinned XSD validates the document. Its
little-endian float32 payload was packed independently with Python
`struct.pack('<12f', 1, -2, 4, 8, 16, -32, 64, 128, 3, 5, -7, 11)`.
The shape is (3, 4) and F2 varies fastest. The direct endpoints are
9 and 3 ppm and the indirect endpoints are −100 and 100 Hz. Both use
the last-point convention. The acquisition is synthetic XML context.

SHA-256: `60cb45948fdfceef095596bda61b2efaf6a2f3f46c1cdef33019a1b5b339023c`.

The official external HSQC example
<https://nmrml.org/examples/6/bmse000400-exp06.nmrML> was inspected locally
(SHA-256 `3231a4769029f362863fb57c7adaaaf6aae304a65c503839b57e5ec02b320f82`).
Its processed array declares zero data points and contains no binary samples.

For raw 2D qualification, download the nmrML example above and extract
`ser`, `acqus`, `acqu2s` and `pulseprogram` from the [BMRB experiment 6 archive](https://bmrb.io/metabolomics/mol_summary/zip_entry_directory.php?experiment=6&id=bmse000400).
The nmrML project publishes the example for format illustration. BMRB
provides the matching archive through entry DOI 10.13018/BMSE000400
(Bruker DMX 500 MHz, XWIN-NMR). Local qualification uses these public
downloads. Redistribution rights for these files have not been assessed.
The files are kept outside the repository. Set `NMRML_HSQC_XML`
and `NMRML_HSQC_SER` to the local paths and run
`python -m pytest tests/interop/test_interop_nmrml_2d.py -k official_hsqc`.

The test compares the complete nmrML FID with the big-endian int32
quadrature words from `ser`. Its SHA-1 is
`a979ed42e5a28066a476557d713c76ce081541da`, matching the nmrML reference.
The source `acqu2s` (SHA-256
`a5f7dde9f300ceda791dc39061d2cca5c341d5206cee2b317828514108a6d50f`)
records `IN[0] = 6.6297935484259e-05` s. The pulse program (SHA-256
`ba9d0d0667cffac7c2db6f7a06135fdda1e168c1e12a1643c277f9dce29a6e14`)
advances the indirect delay after each two-trace cycle. Carbon evolution
contains two d0 delays, so its increment is twice IN[0]. The direct
acquisition status `acqus` (SHA-256
`69fe04b277990aa0076042a012a7549473a5547c12c52c53c0ea30fb22210e1a`)
records `IN[0] = 6.63e-05` s. Twice this value agrees with `1 / SW` from
the nmrML document. The reference uses 132.6 µs per pair. The more precise
value in `acqu2s` differs by about 31 ppm.
